title: Agent Tesla BEC Campaign Uses Emoji-Obfuscated JScript to Steal Credentials From 40+ Apps
content_md: A business email compromise (BEC) campaign targeting finance departments is delivering Agent Tesla v4 through a payment-themed phishing attachment. The malware uses Unicode emoji characters to hide malicious JScript code , then launches the infostealer through a fileless execution chain designed to evade traditional security controls. The campaign impersonates Metropolitan Bank and Trust Company, a legitimate Philippine financial institution. The email resembles a forwarded wire-transfer conversation and urges recipients to review an attached document and respond quickly. This combination of authority, realistic business language and time pressure is designed to persuade finance employees to open the attachment. The file, named “SWIFT Payment Maker 103 – 10.06.26.JS,” is approximately 6.94 MB. Its large size is caused by heavy obfuscation. Hearts, water droplets and other Unicode emoji characters are embedded throughout the script. Windows Script Host ignores these characters during interpretation, allowing the underlying JScript logic to execute while disrupting basic string-based detection and making manual inspection difficult. The sample does not depend on a conventional Base64-and-eval execution pattern or an additional payload download. Sign up and Repeat your Request After execution, the script writes two files to C:\Users\Public\Libraries\ .
